title: April warmth gave no clear repeated apple-versus-cherry flowering progression contrast at 18 Swiss stations in 1996-2023
abstract: We tested whether April warmth changes the time from flowering start to 50 percent flowering by different amounts in apple and cherry. We used 504 complete sets of four dates from 18 fixed Swiss stations in 1996-2023. Four tests covered western and eastern stations in two periods. Models used annual means and controlled March temperature, winter temperature and linear time. Apple-minus-cherry progression slopes were -0.40 to +0.58 days per C. All four adjusted intervals included zero. Alternative error correlation, removal of winter control and exclusion of unusual intervals gave the same uncertain result. Independent reporting delays of zero to one day permit both point-slope signs in all four tests. This bound is a possibility test, not an estimate of date error. Small selected networks, short annual series, unknown visits and weather after some events limit inference. The result does not show equal species responses or a causal climate effect. We test no air pollutant or pollinator mismatch. Code, aggregate evidence, figures, source hashes and reproduction instructions are included.
